content:
marie: Quick UX question — on small-multiples the x-axis labels are collapsing badly at mobile widths. Current behavior is ellipsis + tooltip but screen readers read the truncated label which is confusing.

alex: Yep saw that in the Canary dashboard. The ellipsis hides the unit (ms vs s) which matters for perf graphs.

josh: Do we have the exact breakpoint where this happens? I can repro at 360px with 3 columns.

marie: Repro steps: shrink window to phone width, compare the top-left and bottom-right charts — labels end up like `1.2k…` and tooltip only shows when you hover (not keyboard).

samira: Accessibility nit: keyboard focus should expose the full label and unit. Also voiceover should read the full text. Right now it announces "one point two" which omits 'requests' as the unit.

alex: Thoughts on options: 1) allow axis labels to wrap to two lines and reduce font, 2) keep ellipsis but move unit to a persistent microlabel under the axis, 3) shorten unit to single char (bad).

josh: Prefer option 2 — preserves single-line layout for density, keeps unit visible. Wrapping breaks alignment between charts in a matrix.

marie: Design note: if we do micro-labels, they need an explicit aria-hidden separation so screen readers don't duplicate.

aria-bot: Accessibility checklist: ensure keyboard focus target, ensure aria-label contains full label+unit, ensure tooltip is accessible via focus.

samira: Implementation detail: we should set aria-label="{fullLabel} — unit {unit}" on the axis group and keep visual-only micro-labels aria-hidden.

alex: Also want to avoid adding per-axis DOM elements for perf. Could we reuse existing legend layer for units? Maybe a single overlay that shows units for the currently focused chart.

marie: UX concern: single overlay works for keyboard but not for glance scanning on dashboards. Units are often glanced across multiple charts.

josh: Compromise: micro-label under axis for default view + overlay shown on focus that announces full context. Micro-labels are the single-char or short-form but we include full expansion in aria-label.

marie: For smoothing toggle: some charts apply smoothing by default on small widths which changes peak values and confuses people. We should avoid auto-smoothing unless explicitly requested.

alex: Agreed. Smoothing should be opt-in or at least marked with a visual badge like "Smoothed" and an undo toggle. Users have complained about lost spikes.

samira: Accessibility for smoothing: when smoothing state changes, send a live-region update so screen readers know the chart has changed.

josh: Dev note: we can add a `role=\"status\" aria-live=\"polite\"` update whenever smoothing toggles and include the current smoothing setting.

marie: Outlier handling: there was a request to auto-clip outliers into a separate mini-chart inset. That feels heavy for the compact view. Maybe just add an outlier sentinel marker and a tooltip that explains the clip range.

alex: Sentinel markers + tooltip sounds lightweight. Tooltip should show original value and a small sparkline of the clipped region.

marie: OK next steps: design mock for micro-unit label under axis + visual 'Smoothed' badge; accessibility copy for aria-labels and live region; engineering to prototype sentinel markers.

josh: I'll prototype CSS for micro-labels and keyboard focus. Proposed CSS snippet:```css
.axis-label { display: block; font-size: 11px; color: var(--muted); }
.axis-label--micro { white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis; overflow: hidden; max-width: 48px; }
.chart:focus .axis-tooltip { display: block; }
```

samira: Quick QA checklist item: test with VoiceOver and NVDA at 3 widths (desktop/tablet/mobile) and verify aria-labels read full label+unit.

marie: Will update the Figma and drop mocks in #design-review by EOD. If anyone objects to micro-label + overlay approach speak up here. :thumbsup:

alex: +1 — prefer explicit unit visibility.

josh: +1 from eng, will add prototype branch.

samira: +1 from a11y.

marie: Cool, thanks all. If we hit any perf issues with additional DOM we can revisit.
